items.title: Richard Brunies Interview, 1959-04-27
items.q: played for Mayor Burman's daughter when she made her communion

ctx.x: And, uh, yes. I wondered about coming back, uh, on the way to the funeral, did you play just funeral marches? No, did you ramble? On the way back then you played, didn't he ramble? Jazz music. How far back was that when you had those funerals? Do you remember about how early, how old you were, or when the year would be? I must have been about, 21. You were 21. Yeah. Was that with Papa Jack Lane's band?

No, this was Fish's band. Fish's band played the funerals too. And I played the funerals with Jack too. Jack used to have him on the counter. He was a prophet, you see. He belonged to the prophet. Yeah. Well, there was only one man in the city. How long was that? He had a larger funeral and Grandpa Henry Burman. That was Mayor Martin Burman. Is that right? And that's we, Fisher, and he's there and played for Mayor Burman's daughter when she made her communion over in Algea. That's when he was living. Yes. And he…

That was so long. Well, see, I can think of a few things to ask. I was gonna ask, when you first played with Papa Lane, did you play in his Reliance band, or what was it called? Well, it was the Reliance band.
